notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Local password accounts introduce reusable credentials and session cookies. They must not be accepted over the current plaintext LAN listener, so controller HTTPS or an explicitly documented secure tunnel is a prerequisite for non-loopback account login.

problem: The Worktree Switcher dashboard currently uses plaintext HTTP. Pairing tokens are already sensitive, but adding reusable passwords and browser sessions would make plaintext non-loopback access an unacceptable credential-exposure path.

risk.rollback: Bind the dashboard to loopback and use a secure tunnel. Do not fall back from HTTPS to plaintext LAN password login.

scope: Add optional HTTPS to the Worktree Switcher controller itself, separate from the existing per-project Next.js development HTTPS setting.
Support canonical local key, certificate, and optional CA paths with owner-readable validation; never upload, copy into SQLite, return, or log private-key contents.

Expose effective scheme, certificate mode, bind address, and restart requirement in security settings. Apply listener certificate changes through an explicit controlled controller restart rather than hot-swapping ambiguous state.
Set Secure session cookies and enforce HTTPS-aware Origin validation when Web account mode is used over a non-loopback connection.
Document secure-tunnel and reverse-proxy deployment as alternatives, including how trusted proxy headers are disabled by default and enabled only for an explicit trusted proxy configuration.
source: Security prerequisite identified during local-account design on 2026-08-29
title: Serve the controller dashboard over HTTPS
validation: Serve the dashboard over HTTPS with a configured local certificate and verify API, SSE, pairing, account login, and Secure cookies use the correct origin and scheme.
Verify invalid, missing, unreadable, or mismatched certificate files fail closed without silently starting a plaintext non-loopback account listener.
Verify private-key contents never appear in SQLite, dashboard/API/MCP responses, logs, errors, or process arguments beyond the protected filesystem path contract.
Verify loopback HTTP remains available for local-only operation and a documented secure tunnel can satisfy the non-loopback account transport requirement.
value: Reusable local account credentials and browser sessions can cross the LAN without being exposed as plaintext while local-only users retain a simple loopback setup.
